details.publicNotes:
When carnivorous plants gorge on enough undead flesh, they occasionally develop a strange affinity for necromantic arts. Instead of gobbling up whatever prey they can find, these malevolent mutants hunger for the flesh and vital fluids of sapient creatures. When they find a particularly delectable specimen, they prefer to drain it dry and mummify it, supporting its desiccated flesh with coils of soul-ensnaring vines.

Left undisturbed, corpse flowers have been known to devastate villages and even small towns with their ever-growing armies of undead. Would-be heroes who search the streets of the ruined village for more conventional suspects like undead masterminds or amoral wizards are prone to overlooking the malice that hides within what appears to be nothing more than a particularly foul-smelling flower.

Other than their hordes of loyal vine mummies, corpse flowers are usually solitary, greedy by nature, and unwilling to share in their feasts, even with others of their own kind. Some horror stories tell of entire groves of corpse flowers working in tandem to wipe cities off the map overnight. If these stories are true, none have lived to tell the tale.

Cunning Vines

Though their intelligence is alien to that of most humanoids, the fact that corpse flowers aren't merely mindless plants makes them all the more terrifying. The flowers seem to understand that they might go hungry if their predations are discovered, and thus they make efforts to hide themselves, sometimes underground or in plain sight in gardens or conservatories. Though corpse flowers can't speak, there have been rare reports of specimens that communicate through gestures (or even crude attempts at writing) made by the zombies they create.

Requirements The corpse flower is adjacent to a creature that they killed with their corpse pollen in the last 24 hours

Effect The corpse flower spends 10 minutes to ritually wrap the corpse in their vines, drink the liquids out of their body, and reanimate it as an independent vine mummy under their command. A vine mummy has the statistics of a mummy guardian, except it is mindless and lacks the Blighted Consumption reaction. Vine mummies are not minions, but they have a vague understanding of their creator's will, allowing them to follow their creator, stand guard over a location, or attack their creator's enemies.
